sections.overview: This tanager occurs across parts of the western Amazon basin, from Colombia and Ecuador through Peru to northern Bolivia and Brazil.
sections.identification: The male has vivid crimson plumage set against a black face and throat; the female is less strongly contrasted.
sections.habitat: It is associated with Amazonian lowlands, including seasonally flooded forest and river-edge vegetation.
sections.diet: The species is classified as omnivorous in comparative bird-trait datasets.
sections.behavior: Field records document it in mixed Amazonian bird communities, but the consulted sources provide little species-specific behavioral detail.
sections.reproduction: The sources consulted here do not provide a sufficiently specific account of its breeding to summarize safely.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Ramphocelus, a South American tanager genus whose species include the silver-beaked tanager.
sections.conservation: BirdLife and Oiseaux.net list it as Least Concern.
